Step 1 Codebase Review & Analysis

Deep Understanding

3 · Review Bob's Analysis

Bob provides comprehensive insights for the ModResorts application:

  • Architecture: Monolithic J2EE application with servlets, filters, and JMX MBeans
  • Tech Stack: Java 8, WebSphere Application Server Traditional (tWAS), JSP, servlets, JMX, Maven
  • Dependencies: WebSphere-specific APIs, custom security implementations, legacy patterns
  • Technical Debt: Tight coupling to WebSphere, custom trust managers, hardcoded configurations
  • Code Quality: Mixed patterns, some deprecated APIs, opportunity for modernization
  • Security Issues: Custom SSL implementations, permission handling that needs review

Step 2 Modernization Planning

Strategic Roadmap
The Challenge: Creating a modernization strategy requires balancing business continuity, technical risk, and resource constraints. Wrong decisions can lead to failed migrations and wasted investment.

Try It Yourself

1 · Define Modernization Requirements

P Use Plan Mode for this prompt You're designing a strategy and architecture — no code is written yet. 
Create a modernization plan to:
- Migrate from Java 8 to Java 21
- Convert monolith to microservices architecture
- Replace JSP with React frontend
- Move from Oracle to PostgreSQL
- Deploy on Kubernetes
- Implement CI/CD pipeline
- Zero downtime during migration

2 · Review the Modernization Roadmap

Bob generates a phased approach with risk mitigation:

1 Foundation Weeks 1–2
  • Upgrade to Java 21, Spring Boot 3.x
  • Implement comprehensive test suite (unit, integration)
  • Externalize configurations to environment variables
  • Set up CI/CD pipeline with automated testing
Risk: Low — backward compatible changes
2 Data Layer Weeks 3–4
  • Abstract data access with JPA/Hibernate
  • Create database migration scripts (Oracle → PostgreSQL)
  • Implement dual-write pattern for zero-downtime migration
  • Validate data consistency with automated checks
Risk: Medium — requires careful data validation
3 Service Decomposition Weeks 5–8
  • Identify bounded contexts and service boundaries
  • Extract microservices: User Service, Order Service, Inventory Service
  • Implement API Gateway and service mesh
  • Add distributed tracing and monitoring
Risk: High — requires careful orchestration
4 Frontend Modernization Weeks 9–10
  • Build React SPA with TypeScript
  • Implement RESTful APIs for frontend consumption
  • Add authentication with OAuth2/OIDC
  • Progressive migration with feature flags
Risk: Low — independent of backend changes
5 Cloud Deployment Weeks 11–12
  • Containerize all services with Docker
  • Deploy to Kubernetes with Helm charts
  • Implement auto-scaling and health checks
  • Set up monitoring with Prometheus/Grafana
Risk: Medium — requires infrastructure expertise

Before & After Comparison

Legacy Code — Java 8 + JDBC
public class UserDAO {
    public User getUser(int id) {
        Connection conn = null;
        PreparedStatement stmt = null;
        ResultSet rs = null;
        try {
            conn = DriverManager.getConnection(DB_URL, USER, PASS);
            stmt = conn.prepareStatement(
                "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?");
            stmt.setInt(1, id);
            rs = stmt.executeQuery();
            if (rs.next()) {
                User user = new User();
                user.setId(rs.getInt("id"));
                user.setName(rs.getString("name"));
                user.setEmail(rs.getString("email"));
                return user;
            }
        } catch (SQLException e) {
            e.printStackTrace();
        } finally {
            // Manual resource cleanup
        }
        return null;
    }
}
Modernized Code — Java 21 + Spring Boot
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/users")
@Validated
public class UserController {
    private final UserRepository userRepository;

    public UserController(UserRepository userRepository) {
        this.userRepository = userRepository;
    }

    @GetMapping("/{id}")
    public ResponseEntity<UserDTO> getUser(
            @PathVariable @Positive Long id) {
        return userRepository.findById(id)
            .map(UserDTO::fromEntity)
            .map(ResponseEntity::ok)
            .orElse(ResponseEntity.notFound().build());
    }
}

@Repository
interface UserRepository extends JpaRepository<User, Long> {
    Optional<User> findByEmail(String email);
}

record UserDTO(Long id, String name, String email) {
    static UserDTO fromEntity(User user) {
        return new UserDTO(user.getId(),
            user.getName(), user.getEmail());
    }
}

Transformation Summary

38% reduction — 45 lines → 28 lines
Modern patterns — Records, Optional, Stream API, DI
Security — SQL injection eliminated, input validation added
Maintainability — Separation of concerns, testable components
Performance — Connection pooling, JPA caching, optimized queries

Bob Generates Tests

@SpringBootTest
@AutoConfigureMockMvc
class UserControllerTest {
    @Autowired
    private MockMvc mockMvc;

    @MockBean
    private UserRepository userRepository;

    @Test
    void getUser_WhenExists_ReturnsUser() throws Exception {
        User user = new User(1L, "John Doe", "john@example.com");
        when(userRepository.findById(1L)).thenReturn(Optional.of(user));

        mockMvc.perform(get("/api/users/1"))
            .andExpect(status().isOk())
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.name").value("John Doe"))
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.email").value("john@example.com"));
    }

    @Test
    void getUser_WhenNotExists_Returns404() throws Exception {
        when(userRepository.findById(999L)).thenReturn(Optional.empty());

        mockMvc.perform(get("/api/users/999"))
            .andExpect(status().isNotFound());
    }

    @Test
    void getUser_WithInvalidId_Returns400() throws Exception {
        mockMvc.perform(get("/api/users/-1"))
            .andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
    }
}
